Q: How can I make my tangent numbers generating class resumable? A:

I'm not familiar with that sequence, but the comments on that OEIS entry mention that this sequence can be derived from full binary trees, which indicated to me that the sequence can probably be described using a recurrence relation:

from collections.abc import Generator
from functools import lru_cache
from itertools import count, islice
from math import comb

@lru_cache(None)
def tan(n: int) -> int:
    if n == 1:
        return 1

    s = 0
    for k in range(1, n):
        s += comb(2*n - 2, 2*k - 1) * tan(k) * tan(n - k)

    return s


def tangent_numbers() -> Generator[int, None, None]:
    yield from (tan(n) for n in count(1))


it = tangent_numbers()

print(f"The first term is {next(it)}")
print(f"The second term is {next(it)}")
print(f"The next three after that are {tuple(islice(it, 3))}")

Output:

The first term is 1
The second term is 2
The next three after that are (16, 272, 7936)

tan(n) computes (and caches) the nth term of the sequence, which has the side-effect of computing (and caching) the [1, n) th terms, too.

tangent_numbers is a generator that yields the terms of the sequence, starting at n=1. Using a generator in this way allows for the "resuming" behavior you were describing, where you can consume any number of terms from the generator, and resume execution of the generator at a later time by consuming more terms. The generator is lazy and will compute terms on-demand.

Dunno how this implementation compares to yours in terms of performance, as I haven't tested it, but I assume it's quite speedy thanks to the memoization/cache - especially as n grows.

Q: How to format invalid xml in Notepad++? A:

XML Pretty printers can only deal with vaid XML. Use NotePad++ Plugin 'XML Fools, Select only the text within the CData, and format only that (Valid XML).

Q: Android Toolbar to appear at the bottom of the screen instead of the top A:

Android toolbar is the new Action Bar. It’s not bound to any activity, meaning it can be placed anywhere in the layout, is highly customize-able and can be used as an “Action Bar”.

Details with the code here

XML Layout code

<RelativeLayout
    xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android"
    xmlns:tools="http://schemas.android.com/tools"
    android:layout_width="match_parent"
    android:layout_height="wrap_content"
    android:orientation="vertical"
    tools:context="com.ahotbrew.toolbar.MainActivity">

    <include
        layout="@layout/toolbar"
        android:layout_width="match_parent"
        android:layout_height="wrap_content"
        android:layout_alignParentBottom="true"/>

    <RelativeLayout
        android:layout_width="match_parent"
        android:layout_height="wrap_content"
        android:padding="16dp">

        <TextView
            android:text="@string/hello_brew"
            android:layout_width="wrap_content"
            android:layout_height="wrap_content"/>
    </RelativeLayout>
</RelativeLayout>
